question: to the Commission Dick Erixon (ECR) Subject:

The Commission has announced the winners of the 2026 European Union Prize for Literature1. The winner of the Grand Prix receives EUR 10 000 and financial support for two translations. The two special mention recipients receive EUR 5 000 each and support for one translation each. In addition, the other shortlisted authors receive support for one translation, and all shortlisted authors are promoted at major book fairs in Europe. The prize is an annual part of the Creative Europe programme. In this context: 1.

Can the Commission provide an account of the total budgetary impact of the 2026 literature prize and a full list of all other prizes awarded by the institution, including the budget impact of each prize (total cost of the prize, including the production of awards/diplomas/medals and, for prize ceremonies, logistical support, award panel or jury costs, promotional costs and any other costs)?
How does the Commission justify EU taxpayers financing these types of action while their cost of living is increasing?
https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/mex_26_1216.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (9.9.2026) The Commission is committed to supporting European artists and Europe’s cultural heritage at a time when platforms are becoming ever more powerful and tend to promote nonEuropean culture. This makes it more difficult for European artists and heritage to remain visible to European citizens. One important way of strengthening the visibility of European culture is through the various cultural prizes awarded by the EU. These prizes are co-funded by the Creative Europe Programme. In practice, the Programme supports the prizes through lump-sum grants awarded to the organisations and consortia responsible for managing them. This support is set out in the annual work programmes. For the year 2026, the total amounts corresponding to the awards are: - EU Prize for Popular and Contemporary Music: EUR 600 000 - EU Prize for Contemporary Architecture: EUR 500 000 - European Union Prize for Literature (EUPL): EUR 600 000 - EU Prize for Cultural Heritage: EUR 450 000 - EU Prize for Jewish Cultural Heritage: EUR 300 000 The total amount of co-financing for prizes for 2026 is EUR 2.45 million, representing 0.64% of the Creative Europe budget for that year. The Creative Europe Programme amounts to about 0.23% of the total EU budget for 2021–2027. The prizes are implemented by organisations active in the respective sectors, helping to ensure that prize activities serve the interests of the artists and cultural stakeholders concerned. They are also accompanied by promotion and market-development efforts. For example, winners and nominated authors of the EU Prize for Literature are actively promoted at major book fairs, helping to secure translation rights and broaden international visibility.
